We had an extremely disappointing time @vientianecafe in #westphilly. Circumstances were extenuating, so we may give it another try since it’s a fav of a friend couple of ours. Let’s get to the food:

We had 1 dish in the #restaurant. The fresh tofu spring rolls $7 were excellent and #glutenfree. They were soft and the sauce was a very nice compliment to the sticky fresh rolls. Soft rice paper with herbs and vermicelli, served with tangy tamarind and sweet chili sauce topped with crushed peanuts.  Get shrimp for $8. 

Then, our takeout portion included the gf Laotian Homemade Sausages (sai-gawk) $17. These were pretty good but had too much stuff inside the sausages when I’m lookin for something like an Italian sausage or bratwurst. Prob my problem since it’s an expectation thing.  The 2 sauces were extremely hot!! Stuffed with chopped pork, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves; served with steam vegetables along with spicy roasted chili garlic sauce (jeow muk phet) and sticky rice.  It was def solid with #takeout. 

We also ate the #gf tofu Banh-Xeo $13. It was an Asian crepe stuffed with beansprouts, onions and carrots, scallions and served with house sauce.
This was ok. Too many crunchy veggies in it for me but I liked it more than other savory pancake/#crepe type foods I’ve tried. Def good quality even with the takeout order. 

Finally we got the gf mango sticky rice $10 to go as well. It was fine. This prob is way better in restaurant. The white sauce was so sweet and good!

So our issue was that we ordered the 2 apps quickly, then the entree and dessert soon after and the dishes just never came out. We had somewhere to be in 20 min and the wait staff prob was waiting for the crepes to bring everything out.  We told them after 20 min we needed to leave if food wasn’t coming out right now; they slow rolled for 5 min saying it was coming out and after 10 min nothing came, so we got up to leave and pay for the 1 thing we ate.  Then at the counter they couldn’t figure out what was ready and not and kept asking if we wanted the other dishes we ordered. Pretty insane.

caption:
if you love the taste of the rice at the bottom of your pan and you love mangoes, you should not miss out on trying the mango sticky rice from Chon Tong Thai Kitchen and Dessert!

The initial taste is a hint of slightly crispy browned rice from the bottom of the pan, and then you’re hit with the sweetness of the coconut cream sauce. And they pair so well together. The mangoes they had with this meal was perfectly ripe and sweet. 

I ordered one bowl and immediately had to turn around and get another. ive had this twice since then and the quality of it has been consistent and amazing each time. If that doesn’t convince you, i’m not sure what will! 

Go get some delicious mango sticky rice and let me know how happy it makes you!

7327. “I think, similar to restaurants, people enjoy architecture for the beauty of the thing.”
-
Though he was raised in the D.C. area, Daniel McLaughlin often visited family in West Philly as a kid. Therefore, figuring it’d be nice to be close to them for college, he studied Architecture at @drexeluniv. But after graduating, Daniel worked as a server alongside opening a woodworking business with his friend.
-
They produced custom furniture for interior designers; however, after his friend moved away, Daniel shifted his focus to the restaurant world. He became the GM of @phloysterhouse and 5 years later opened @missiontaqueria upstairs!
-
Ironically, he’d celebrated his 21st birthday in the space when it was Nodding Head Brewery, but after a multi year renovation his vision came to life. Since 2016, Daniel’s found success not only through running a great restaurant, but through leveraging his creativity.
-
From 2017-2019 he hosted monthly TACOLABs (collaborations with local chefs), in 2019 he hosted a Friendsgiving potluck fundraiser for 150 people, during Covid he operated out of the parking garage across the street and just recently he began hosting Free Association dinners - free dinners for total strangers to meet!
-
Nowadays, he’s even creating content to teach others how to get into running a restaurant. Yet ultimately, Daniel’s just shooting for a sense of peace - something he finds in yoga, in shows like @lctheater’s Ragtime and in meaningful connections with the community! Awesome hanging with you, @missiontaqueria!
•
How we met: I saw @el.brisk’s @phillymag article on Daniel’s dinners and then DM’ed him to meet!

🎶 I'm a fool to do your dirty work... but somebody's gotta do it. 

🚮 Let's talk about trash collection. Everybody wants to design the cute stuff, but it pays to design the ugly stuff too. Restaurants are inherently wasteful businesses, and all that waste has gotta go somewhere. 

🗑️ This typically involves hiring a private waste management company to pick up your trash, but how much trash are we talking? How big should the container be, and how many containers do you need? Where will you put them that doesn't interfere with your neighbors, but are still accessible? How many days a week do you need them to be picked up??

😵‍💫 See?! Not so simple. That's not even factoring in added costs like recycling, compost, or used fryer oil collection. All of which cost money.

♻️ A healthy system of any kind is one that considers the output as much as the input. It might be ugly, but you gotta be sure to put some effort into that when designing your own business.

What's in a name?! 🌹💩 

📣 When naming your restaurant or small business, you have to think of it like naming your dog. You're gonna be introducing that pup to everyone for the rest of its life, saying its name out loud, and writing it on every piece of paperwork.

🪙 Loans vs Investors! 🪙 There's definitely
pros and cons to both...

🏦 Getting a business loan with a bank is a lot like getting a mortgage. They're gonna wanna see proof of assets or income to cover the principle and interest payments on the loan. If you can't prove that, you might have to go with...

🤝 Investors. They're gonna wanna see a business plan that shows your investment is more lucrative than a traditional investment, like the stock market. Investors are often people you're close with, like friends or family. And when has mixing money into those relationships ever gone wrong?! 😬 

🤓 My advice to you is to try and open your restaurant as light and lean as possible. Approach the SBA (Small Business Administration) about a loan cause their terms are often kinder than a traditional bank. Was the interest payments, grow your brand, and hopefully pay it down quickly as you grow. 🌱

The 5 Year Restaurant Timeline.
(Abridged version 🗓️)

1️⃣ The first year is the hardest. You're working crazy hours. You're not sleeping much. You have this newborn business baby that needs constant care and attention. 👶🏻 

2️⃣ You survive the first year! (or at least it doesn't end you 🤯) Now you can correct all the mistakes you made in year one! Refine your systems, edit your offerings, and look back at everything you learned from your first year to help you grow. 

3️⃣ Year 3 is about building community. You get all your hot press in your first year or two, cause you're the new kid on the block. But once there's no more headlines, how do you prove to your community that you're more than a flash in a pan?

4️⃣ Consistency! You've had 3 years to learn what your customers want from you. Now you just gotta keep delivering it again and again and again. 

5️⃣ Year Five is about YOU! At this point your restaurant is in business kindergarten! You can hopefully leave it in capable hands for the most part. So how do you want to be in or out of the day to day operations?

The simple menu. paper 🔖 Not so simple reallly...

📜 It can be so easy to overlook the choices that go into making a restaurant's menu. Is it paper? In a sleeve? A binder? A leather book? Projected on a wall? Written on a chalkboard? Or do you scan in on a QR code?

🥶 Let's take a tour of something restaurants never show you: their walk-in refrigerator! 👀 

🕵🏻‍♂️ Looking inside someone's fridge is almost like looking through their bedside table. It says a lot about them lol. What do they eat, what brands do they prefer, how clean is it, is there anything rotting? (I'm talking about the bedside table obvi 😜)

👀 But in a restaurant it says so much about how a place cares for its product. We are charged with public safety after all, and get regular inspections by the health department. If things are stored improperly, it can create a dangerous situation.

📝 There are many rules in how to properly stock a walk in, but here's 5 quick hits:

1.  FIFO! First in, first out. You don't want anything getting old in there. 

2.  Nothing on the floor ever! Your lowest shelves have to be at least 6" off the ground. 

3. Proteins get tiered in order of their cooking temperature, so the things with the highest temps (like poultry) go on the lowest shelf, and things like fish go on higher shelves. 

4. Everything has to be labeled and dated. 

5. The temp must be held between 33°-39° which is just above freezing, but just below "the danger zone." 🦠

👨‍⚖️ I'm not a lawyer, but I can spell LLC! What
@davidchang and @stephen.starr are talking about is the danger of personally financing your restaurant.

🤑 When forming your restaurant or small business, it might seem easiest to finance things through a personal loan. Which is all fine and good, but you'll want to be sure the loan is structured through an LLC.

👨‍🏫 LLC stands for Limited Liability Company, so it literally limits your liability in case your business fails.
Whatever you do, DO NOT sign a personal guarantee. That means that you will be personally held responsible for whatever debt, back rent, interest, penalties and collection costs that might remain after your LLC shudders.

💥 Even if you have an LLC, a personal guarantee will legally supersede that, and leave you vulnerable to having your car, house, or other assets possessed, and/or garnishments against future wages until the debt is paid back.

🙋‍♂️ It is supremely important you consult a business lawyer to go over any loan documents or legal paperwork before. you. sign. ANYTHING!!

5 things they don't tell you... 🫣

5️⃣ You will never be home on time, ever. Just when you think you're done, something will need your immediate attention and keep you there unexpectedly, so start to expect the unexpected. 

4️⃣ Even though you serve people hot meals all day long, you'll be eating most of YOUR meals cold, standing up in the dish pit. 

3️⃣ Even though you never leave the same room, you'll walk 5-7 miles a day just going back and forth. Clock your steps. It's crazy. 

2️⃣ When your customers are off, that means you're on! So expect to be working nights and weekends, but DON'T expect to be home for the holidays. 

1️⃣ When you're the restaurateur, you are permanently on call. So that thing you've been looking forward to for months? There's a 50/50 shot that something will go wrong and ruin your plans.

🤔 Did you know that 9 out of 10 restaurants fail in their 1st year? Wait, how do you know that? Is that even true?!

📺 I've heard this stat quoted plenty in my
restaurant career, and apparently this falsehood is traced back to a 2003 Amex commercial featuring Rocco DiSpirito who, at the time, was promoting his show The Restaurant.

📝 Here are the facts: According to a study by the Bureau of Labor & Statistics (back when we trusted the BLS lol) only 17% of restaurants fail in their first year. This is based on data that surveyed 81,000 independently owned full service restaurants over 20 years!

🗓️ In fact, restaurants have a median life span of 4.5 years, which is longer than other service businesses that offer janitorial services, or computer software assistance.

🤷‍♂️ Yet, there's this pervasive belief that restaurants are risky startups. That's due to many other factors of course, that I go into here. BUT when you hear stats like this, don't be dissuaded. Do your market research instead of buying into the hype.

If you can't stand the heat... Check out our kitchen when we're closed! 😏

🧑‍🍳 Kitchen design is so important when concepting your menu. This may seem obvious, but if you want fried things, you'll need a fryer! If you want grilled things, you'll need a grill! All those pieces of equipment take up space, so just make sure you have enough room for everything, or you might have to make some menu edits. ✂️ 

🔥 Any gas, or wood burning equipment needs to be vented, so you'll need to make sure it fits under your exhaust hood. A hood is one of the most expensive components of a kitchen build out! So the shorter your line, the shorter the price tag. 🏷️ 

😷 You also want to be mindful of areas where cross contamination might occur. Keeping things like raw veg, away from raw shellfish is just common sense for safety operations.

🗓️ Let's talk about hours of operation. It can be tempting when opening your business to be available as many hours of the week as possible, to make as much money as possible. After all, you're not making any money when you're closed.

🚷 BUT there are definitely benefits to limiting your hours, or even reserving a day or two a week to fully close. It allows your employees to get a break, you're building to get a break, and YOU to get a break.

🔛 As a business owner, you're kind of always ON. It's a relief to know there is some time each week where absolutely nothing can go wrong, because no one is there to create any problems!!

Wake up , wake up, it's the first of tha mooonnthhh! RENT! They seem to want it like, every 30 days! What's up with that...

🏨 The industry standard for restaurant rent is between 6-10% of your monthly gross sales. This can be less if you're a fast casual restaurant, or more if you're a full service restaurant in a prime location. 

📉 One of the main reasons restaurants fail is poor lease negotiation. If you lock yourself in to a high rate at the onset, you could be chasing that number every month. 

🤝 Some landlords are open to percentage rent, where you pay a percentage of your monthly sales for a year or two so you can establish a baseline revenue, then fix in a rate from there. 

💍 DO NOT let some developer talk you into "the perfect space." If the math doesn't math, have the confidence to walk away.

1 INVENTORY, wahaha 🧛‍♂️ It's time to practice
those counting skills bbs!

🗓️ The last day of the month is when most restaurants will do an in-house accounting of everything they have on hand. Even that jar of capers you bought for a brunch special 3 years ago. It still counts as something you purchased, but haven't yet sold.

🧮 It's important to do inventory on a regular interval (monthly/weekly) to keep eyes on your product, watch out for waste, usage (and theft 😬) It's also important to know how much product you have in hand cause that product has a value which if it's not sold, just comes off your bottom line.

👨‍🏫 Your cost of goods (or COGS) is determined by this simple formula: Beginning Inventory + Purchases - Ending Inventory. You then divide that number by your monthly sales, and you've got your Food Cost. Yay math!

@surayaphilly review…

It is with a heavy heart that I write this but I was incredibly disappointed by Suraya. I have been looking for an opportunity to try this spot for months and I was very excited to try their brunch with my mom during her visit to Philly. Stunning interior, great choice of color and lighting and wonderful service. That was the best part of our meal. At no point was my water glass less than half way filled. 

The dips (hummous, labneh, muhammara, etc) took longer than they should have to arrive to the table and were all quite underwhelming. The pita was freshly baked, pillowy and delicious. We ordered the kafta kebab, shakshuka, and grilled branzino. At no point in the meal did I think to myself “wow, that’s tasty.” I felt that there were some pretty key technique or timing related flaws. The kafta was overcooked and lacked moisture. The yolk of the shakshuka was fully cooked through which docked a significant amount of points for me. The branzino had a wonderfully crisp skin which mostly redeemed the dish but otherwise was not particularly notable. Nothing about the meal spoke to me and I really hate to say it but it felt like nothing more than significantly overpriced sustenance at the end of the day. On our way out, we picked up a pistachio crueller which was pretty fantastic but hadn’t the slightest hint of pistachio flavor besides a dusting of pistachio crumbles on top. 

At $42 a person for the (mandatory) brunch tasting menu it is simply not worth the price. The attention to detail seems to lie more in the aesthetics of the interior than in the food itself. While “heart broken” does seem a bit dramatic to say, I am struggling to find better words that encapsulate my feelings about this meal. I want to believe that I caught the kitchen on an off day and that maybe there is some truth to the Michelin recommendation. Based off of my experience, I’m having a hard time finding what would have given them that status. I was so ready to fall in love with Suraya as I have with other restaurants within the @dhrestaurants collection but just can’t. Feeling super #sad :(

~Ancestral Old Fashioned~

This is an elevated take on an old fashioned, made with Cascahuin Reposado Private Batch, and Siembra Valles Ancestral. It highlights the terroir of the valles region of Jalisco, and it pays a tribute to the Cascahuin distillery and the long relationship between the Rosales and the Suro families.

Cascahuin Reposado is a private batch made for Tequilas and Mirate restaurant in LA, a highproof tequila rested for 6 months in ex jack danielas barrels. 

Siembra Valles Ancestral Tequila is produced in the Cascahuin distillery by master distiller Salvador Rosales Torres. Using ancestral methods of production commonly used by early distillers, like agave cooked in earth pits, hand wood mallets maceration and distillation in Filipino style pine wood still! @siembraspirits @cascahuin @edith_m_ramirez @dan_suro @eduardo_moreno519 @dave_suro_jr @davidsurop @concerned.citizen @the_0ne_above_all @victor.gallo86 @rachelore_ #oaxacaoldfashioned #oldfashioned #tequilasphilly #tequilascasamexicana
Celebrating Julie’s birthday!!

We introduce to you: the ~Magueyero~

A spirt forward and herbal cocktail made with, Cascahuin Blanco infused with pápalo. Faccia Brutto Centerbe, Dolan blanc, and dandelion bitters.

Pápalo is an herb endemic from central Mexico and South America. It has a complex taste of mint, citrus, cilantro; pungent with a slightly soapy. 

This cocktail honors the bat magueyero, a species that is responsable for the natural reproduction of agaves through pollination.

Philly’s great new cocktail bar: Milpa at @lajefaphilly! 

A quick explainer: @tequilasphilly, Rittenhouse’s long-running Mexican restaurant recently reopened after a fire and renovation. A second venue in the back, @lajefaphilly, came with it — all day cafe and bar vibes. Within La Jefa (bright, casual), Milpa Bar offers a different cocktail menu and atmosphere (dark, luxe), but the same menu as La Jefa.

Modern Mexican is on the menu, with ceviche, lots of fun fried fare, a couple of entrees, excellent sauces and purées, and a good amount of vegetarian-friendly dishes.

The cocktails here are really special — each completely unique, with unexpected ingredients, glassware, and one with the clearest ice cube I’ve ever seen.

🙋🏾‍♂️ If you find yourself in the Phila Tri State Area and you're looking for an *Authentic* Mexican experience, I'll save you some time AND set you up for success....

In the lead-up to Christmas, we wanted to gift ourselves a moment of calm, flavor, and beauty — so we headed to a festive afternoon tea ✨
This is not just a dessert set, but a true ritual where every detail feels thoughtfully curated 🤍

The tea experience @roamlic is presented as an elegant set combining refined desserts and delicate savory bites 🍰🥐
The table fills with light mousse cakes, beautifully layered pastries, mini baked goods, and sweets that reflect true pastry craftsmanship. Everything is subtle, well-balanced, and never overly sweet — exactly what you crave during the winter season ❄️✨

The tea itself is a highlight 🍵
Fragrant, deep, and perfectly paired with the desserts, it’s served hot and meant to be savored slowly. It’s not just about taste, but about the experience: unhurried moments, quiet conversations, and the joy of slowing down 🤍

The entire tea service is built around a feeling of warmth and celebration ✨
Soft lighting, elegant presentation, and a sense that you’re in a space created with genuine care and love for detail. This is not a place for a quick bite, but for truly living the moment 🌙🕯️

We enjoyed every bite and every sip 🤍
You can feel the respect for ingredients, flavor, and the guest experience. That’s why Anntremet offers some of the most delicious desserts in New York 🍰✨

If you’re looking to soak in a festive atmosphere, take a beautiful pause, and enjoy a refined tea experience — this is a place you shouldn’t miss 🎄✨

ABV15% 

Annual release of the nama version of gokujo no kire. Nose of charcuterie, smoke, baijiu and melon. Smooth sweetness balanced with muted acidity and alcohol dryness, ending with a palette cleansing finish. 

I rarely get charcuterie notes from newly released Nama (this one was released from Shuzo in November 2025), and based on back label information it was made with extremely low temp fermentation. Curious where that smoked dried meat aroma is from - is it that 結の香- Iwate’s local rice used a lot by Akabu, when milled to 35%, has larger amounts of proteins compared to other rice varieties?

At MercatoLIC, hospitality isn’t just something we say — it’s who we are.
From the moment you walk through our doors, our goal is simple: to make you feel welcome, comfortable, and truly taken care of.

Our food is inspired by Italy, made with care, and meant to be shared — from fresh pasta and wood-fired pizza to a great glass of wine poured just the way you like it.
But what really sets us apart is the people.

Our owner, Gino, is always here — greeting guests, checking in, making sure everything feels just right. Whether it’s your first visit or your hundredth, you’re never just a table number here. You’re family.

So take your time. Enjoy the moment. Laugh a little longer.

Our meal at @spicefinchphilly did not disappoint. We discovered this restaurant while researching places that Top Chef contestants have been involved with, and Jenn Carroll used to be executive chef here and is now a silent partner. 
Spice Finch is a Mediterranean place with heavy influences from North Africa. 
- I got to try an orange wine for the first time and would love to explore other ones. 
- The mezze platter consisted of garlic yogurt (lemon, Aleppo pepper, evoo), red pepper hummus, melitzanosalata (a combination of eggplant, feta, bell pepper, walnuts, pomegranate, and mint), crudités, and herb oil flatbread. 
- After my big lunch, I felt like a salad for dinner, so I opted for the baby green salad, which was on a bed of the lemon yogurt, and had pomegranate and apples, along with a savory and smoky dressing. Tasted like bacon, oddly enough. 
- For dessert, we tried their olive oil cake, with orange blossom water, candied orange, and powdered sugar. Not the texture we expected but a very enjoyable and fresh flavor. 
The service was awesome and attentive, as well as being knowledgeable about the food. Overall, would recommend Spice Finch if you’re ever in Philadelphia and want some Mediterranean with a unique twist.

Spice Finch is a flavor-packed gem in Philly ✨

From the fruit & feta to the chickpea wedges, green hummus, and shabazi fries! everything was insanely good. The trio of spreads hit every note, and the duck wings, halibut, chicken, and roasted beets were all cooked to perfection.

And let’s talk about the Sunstone Elixir… that cocktail alone is worth the visit 🍹so refreshing and beautifully balanced.

Definitely one of my favorite Mediterranean spots in the city right now! Go check out @spicefinchphilly

I heard such good things about Spice Finch, so me and my two best friends went for happy hour and loved every second! We started out with mocktails and cocktails, but Spice Finch also has beer and wine on their Happy Hour menu. We had to get the Shabazi Flatbread, the Duo of Spreads, and the Shabazi Fries to start. The hummus was amazing and the garlic yogurt was tangy and delightful, but the harissa aioli they served with the fries was addicting. We then proceeded to get every single small plate… 😬 because why not! Favorites were definitely the Duck Wings, the Chickpea Wedges, and the Lamb Merguez. Spice Finch’s Happy Hour is available at their bar and outside tables Monday-Friday from 4pm-6pm & Saturday-Sunday from 3pm-5pm. When you go, do not skip the Chickpea Wedges, & be sure to tell ‘em PFAB sent ya!
📍220 South 17th Street Philadelphia PA 19103📍

i am obsessed with the tahini brownie dessert from @spicefinchphilly
•
I don’t repeat restaurants multiple times very often, but I’ve been to Spice Finch a few times & it’s been so consistently good over the years. Particularly, the tahini brownie, which is on my list of my favorite desserts from a philly restaurant. I hope it never leaves the menu
•
I like that it’s a great vibe inside & always feels buzzing since its in a prime center city location & connected to a hotel, but also always feels possible to get a bar stool, grab a table in the bar area or maybe make a last minute reservation. We walked in at prime time Saturday night & got a table in the bar area with full service from the bartender, so it was essentially  a normal table
•
Everything we ordered we liked but especially the pasta small plate which included a type of pasta I wasn’t familiar with before, Nwassar. Super thin, flat, postage stamp sized pasta squares – sort of like one side of a ravioli that just was never connected to its other half. It’s a type of pasta from Tunisia, which is just super interesting to me as a food nerd. Anyway, this dish also included mushrooms, brussel sprouts, sunchokes and manchego and we were fighting over every last bite.
•
The duck wings with pomegranate BBQ sauce are also worth mentioning. The way that their pomegranate BBQ sauce tastes is everything I am expecting when I hear that something is going to be glazed in pomegranate. Super bold and delicious flavor. I absolutely love the duck and lamb dishes here, both sticky with pomegranate sauces
•
Last but not least to specifically make note of is the espresso martini, which isn’t listed on the menu, but of course they make one. This one was really good with strong coffee flavor, not sweet or sugary and of course 3 beans. I am still in my espresso martini era and back on my game of trying from as many places as I can this year, and this is in my top tier.
•
Go here for excellent food and a buzzing atmosphere in center city
•

New Delhi Indian Restaurant. Philadelphia, PA. 🇮🇳 Choices, choices, choices! Generally, for me, a bad thing. I need focus, I need streamlined, I need someone else to tell me what I need. But there is one arena where more is truly merrier: the all-you-can-eat buffet. And there’s nowhere I’d rather eat it all than at New Delhi in Philadelphia. New Delhi is not doing anything off the wall or experimental, they’re just making the Indian cuisine staples you know and love at their most lovable. The chicken tikka is amazing, the chana masala is great, but the korma, a dish I’d normally glaze over on a menu, is the stand-out for me. And I will have all three and then some! I like to create a sauce conglomerate in which to dunk and scoop my naan and rice respectively. My favorite part of the experience, besides walking to the restroom through a fully chrome hallway (FUUUTURE!), is pouring myself a cup of hot milky chai for the road. It’s always the thing that puts my fullness over the edge (like, needing-to-perform-the-show-from-a-gurney edge), but it’s so warming and sweet, I can’t deny myself such a perfect treat. And you shouldn’t either! @newdelhiphilly #foodblogger #illustration #foodillustration #ipadart

Amazing happy hour in Center City alert!!! 🚨 @vedaphilly has some reallllyyyyy delicious cocktails along with their delicious modern Indian bites. The drunken lassi was everything, mango lassi you know and love with a kick of rum, and the Laila was floral & refreshing (and stunning!!) the old fashioned was done very well and smooth and the Karishma was like a slightly spicy tequila mule.

Now onto the food - we had an absolute feast and tried out the entire happy hour menu. The stars of the show had to be the ribs (that glaze is so good), the samosa and the cauliflower - but I’m also partial to the crab cake and fish. If you like goat cheese, that naan is a must try, it was great to scoop up the curry sauces later. Everything was so flavorful and the portions were great.

For the mains, we tried 3 different dishes with garlic naan & basmati rice. My favorite is always Korma and this was no different, creamy, flavorful and not very spicy. 

A seriously great place to get an amazing cocktail and some yummy bites - we’ll be back! Thank you @vedaphilly 🤍

Proof that Philly’s South Street isn’t just about cheesesteaks and late-night pizza slices, it’s also serving up naan-stop vegan flavor 😉.

@indian_kitchen_lovash has vegan options clearly labeled (thank you 🙌), tofu dishes that make you forget tofu’s bad PR, and the choice of cozy dine-in or quick takeout when you want curry on the sofa. 

And behind it all? Award-winning chef Mohan Parmar, a culinary powerhouse who’s been keeping authentic Indian traditions alive since 1983. I think he deserves a standing ovation… but I settled for ordering seconds. 🌶️🍛

So if you’re wandering South Street, skip the usual suspects and let your taste buds take a plant-based trip to India.

Life goes on ….

Regalamos la idea (y la práctica) de una comunidad donde nadie tenga que vivir con miedo. Un hogar donde el amor no duela. Un “te quiero” que no controle. Un “perdón” que no sea trampa. Un país donde ser mujer no sea un riesgo, y donde las niñas crezcan con derechos, no con alertas.

Que esta Navidad nos encuentre sembrando lo que la violencia odia:

De nuestro equipo para ti: gracias por ser parte de esta red que cuida, denuncia, acompaña y transforma.

Y si hoy no se siente “feliz navidad”, también está bien: aquí estamos. No estás sola. No estás solo.

Con amor y lucha,

**Equipo Madre Tierra** 💜✨

@madonna and @nilerodgers at Live Aid on July 13, 1985.

While Nile Rodgers is seen here shredding on guitar during Madonna’s Live Aid set, their professional bond went much deeper. Rodgers actually produced her diamond-certified breakout album, Like a Virgin, just one year earlier in 1984! 🎸✨

Despite the sweltering 90°F heat at JFK Stadium in Philadelphia, Madonna famously refused to take off her patterned coat during this performance. Her reason? She told the crowd, “I’m not taking shit off today! They might hold it against me ten years from now!”—a cheeky nod to the media frenzy surrounding the release of her early modelling photos at the time🧥🔥

Madonna didn’t just perform her own hits like “Holiday” and “Into the Groove” that day. She and Nile Rodgers also joined the Thompson Twins for a high-energy cover of The Beatles’ “Revolution.” This photo captures the duo during one of the most-watched broadcasts in television history, reaching an estimated 1.9 billion people! 🌎📺

Philadelphia Food Guide: Must-Try French Brunch 🇫🇷

@forsythia_philly is easily one of the best ways to start a day in Old City. It was recently added to the Michelin Guide as a recommended spot, and Chef Christopher Kearse is serving up some incredible bold French cooking.

🚶🏻‍♂️I was actually in town to catch Pokémon and needed a solid meal to fuel up before a full day of walking. This spot was the perfect hearty start.

🍳 DISHES FEATURED IN VIDEO

• Beet Pickled Deviled Eggs: stunning color and flavor with lobster bottarga, vadouvan, and lemon ash.

• Steak & Eggs: tender beef paired with a super crisp potato rösti and sauce au poivre that rounds everything out.

• Duck Confit Stuffed Crepe: a savory highlight with caramelized onion, a sunny egg, and black truffle cognac sauce.

• Pain Perdu: The star of the table. Cardamom brioche French toast topped with dark rum chantilly cream, huckleberry marmalade, and hazelnut praline.

✨ Definitely add this to your list if you are visiting Philadelphia. It set me up perfectly for all those kilometers ahead.

📍 233 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia, PA 👇 Share this with your brunch squad!

A huge congratulations to @forsythia_philly and Chef @christopherkearse on earning a coveted spot on this year’s @michelinguide Recommended list last night in Philadelphia!! 👏🏻🌿 Honored doesn’t begin to cover how we feel seeing this project continue to receive the recognition it so deeply deserves.

In the heart of Old City, Forsythia reimagines the French bistro through a modern lens. Dubbed "Best First Date Spot" by @bonappetitmag this space was designed for intimacy, warmth, and the kind of lively conversation where a first dates turn into lifelong love stories. 

Some of the highlights: 

•Handmade zellij tile, sourced from @mosaichousenyc 

•A sculptural globe pendant installation by @cedarandmoss Moss.

•Custom booths, upholstered in a French fabric, paired seamlessly with off-the-shelf furniture from @cb2 and @westelm 

•Acoustical batting and exposed beams that ensure the restaurant maintains its energy without overwhelming noise.

The most unexpected design moment came during demolition when original plaster walls, aged with water stains and exposed lath, were uncovered beneath drywall. Rather than cover them up, we embraced their imperfections, letting the organic patina of time become a defining feature of the space.

Additional layers of texture and history include:

• @williammorriscollection wallpaper, sealed with a matte lacquer for durability.

•A curated mix of original artwork and @hilmaafklintofficial reproductions.

•Floating electrical conduit, adding an industrial yet intentional aesthetic.

A restaurant where every detail tells a story of craftsmanship, character, and connection. And the story continues — We’re honored to be collaborating with Chef Kearse and his team once again on an exciting new concept coming to Philadelphia soon. Stay tuned, something special is on the horizon. ✨🍸

Forsythia, Philadelphia PA:
Came for Forsythia's 6 Year Anniversary dinner.
Tbh, a little disappointed.
Favorites were the cocktail bar snacks, and the dessert.
Rabbit terrine and hen of the woods were fine.
I had high hopes for the Hamachi Kama, but realized that I still prefer to have it grilled, paired with ponzu sauce and daikon oroshi.
Escargot vol-au-vent paired with unagi sauce sounds delicious on paper, but does not work for my palate. It is simply TOO rich: puff pastry (which was cooked to perfection!), plus syrupy sweet sauce. I would prefer some acidity to cut it through, something like a wine based sauce.

Visit count: 7

We’ve been working long and hard on this one, and it’s almost here: our 6th Anniversary! 🥂🍾

We are so excited to take you on a 6-course journey through Chef Christopher Kearse’s culinary career. The menu is designed to highlight major achievements, stand-out dishes, and preludes to the future. Join us on Thursday, August 21st, as we celebrate 6 years of Forsythia with anecdotes of the past and something extra special for those who dine with us that evening. ✨

Make your reservations today via Resy! $105 menu. Menu is also available on our website, or view it in our story.

One of my favorite traditions each year is helping host the Mosaic Development Partners JV holiday party. My career is rooted in celebrating people and progress and this night is always a reflection of the achievements we work toward together all year long.

It was especially meaningful to gather with our team and to welcome some of our partners to celebrate the momentum we have built and the relationships that make the work possible. Moments like this are a reminder that development is about more than projects. It is about people, trust, and shared goals.

Grateful for another strong year and excited for 2026 and the impactful work ahead.

Photo credit: @allmoneyshots

What a great way to close out the year.

Thank you to our partners, collaborators, and friends who joined us for Mosaic Development Partners JV’s holiday party this past Saturday. It was an evening filled with good conversation, meaningful connections, and a lot of gratitude for the work we continue to do together.

We are proud of what we have accomplished this year and even more excited for what is ahead. Wishing everyone a joyful holiday season and continued success in the year to come.

caption:
If you choose to fully enjoy yourself through the holidays and start fresh in January- go for it! 

If you really want to watch what you eat and be mindful mainly to feel your best- then go for it !

If you’re worried about losing progress- I promise you won’t. A few days of celebrations won’t put you behind if you are someone who is normally at least 80% consistent with nutrition and training on the regular and plan to get back to routine after. 

Neither option is “right” or “wrong”. You CHOOSE what is best for YOU. 

And understand- how you feel AFTER is YOUR responsibility. It’s a decision YOU make. 

IMO, you can have best of both worlds❤️ but what you do 80% of the time (all year round) is what is most important to focus on. Not what happens in one week. 

Sending love friends, always😘❤️

Overall, a little pricey but a very cute restaurant.

caption:
If you choose to fully enjoy yourself through the holidays and start fresh in January- go for it! 

If you really want to watch what you eat and be mindful mainly to feel your best- then go for it !

If you’re worried about losing progress- I promise you won’t. A few days of celebrations won’t put you behind if you are someone who is normally at least 80% consistent with nutrition and training on the regular and plan to get back to routine after. 

Neither option is “right” or “wrong”. You CHOOSE what is best for YOU. 

And understand- how you feel AFTER is YOUR responsibility. It’s a decision YOU make. 

IMO, you can have best of both worlds❤️ but what you do 80% of the time (all year round) is what is most important to focus on. Not what happens in one week. 

Sending love friends, always😘❤️

I was staying at the Kimpton Hotel Monaco in Old City, and my friends and I were hungry. So we checked out the menu for the restaurant right downstairs, and as soon as I saw A Carnivore’s Feast, I was sold. The Red Owl Parrillada is a fire-grilled feast inspired by the great steakhouses of South America. This massive meat platter can be served for 2-3 or for 4-5. On the board you have charred NY Strip, Bone-In Short Ribs, Harissa Chicken Thighs, & Crispy Pork Belly, as well as sauces like an olive salsa verde, homemade chimichurri, & some charred lemons & roasted garlic. When this arrived at our table, my mouth was immediately watering. All the meat was cooked exactly how we requested & it was seasoned so well. We loved how wonderfully all the meats paired with the sauces, and the smaller portion size was perfect for our group of 3. We also NEEDED to try the Spicy Crab Noodles, which for sure brought the heat. We also got the Mac and Cheese, which is a MUST here. Honestly, I don’t know why more people aren’t talking about Red Owl Tavern. They have a wonderful beverage program and some truly solid food. I would go back for the Carnivore Feast tomorrow. This was a great deal & perfect for a group! Next time you and your meat loving friends are craving a great meal, check out the Carnivore Feast from Red Owl Tavern, & be sure to tell ‘em PFAB sent ya!

- we clearly ate first, the phone had to wait -
with two locations in the rittenhouse area, marathon has made itself a true staple with good food, good service, and an even better price. read below for our thoughts: 

Dans Score 9/10:
- price: 10/10- solid price for good food made with local ingredients $48 for 2 entrees and a drink
- Ambience 6/10- too bright but otherwise good. The windows make for great people watching. 
- Service- 10/10- attentive but not overbearing server little to no wait time for food. 
- Food- 9/10 really good food. Everything felt very high quality, fries needed salt. Loses one point for having too many options in the menu. 
A solid easy choice, has so many menu options it’s almost overbearing. But that being said it gives you 

Abbie’s Score: 9/10
🤑Price: 10/10 taking in that marathon uses local ingredients and supports local businesses, the price for two was very manageable and a great deal! 
🌟Ambience: 8/10 love the massive windows and they’re great for people watching, but it can be quite loud at times and the lighting is pretty bright. 
📌 Service: 10/10 our server was lovely! he was attentive and checked on us frequently but not so much that it was annoying, and always refilled our waters when they were empty. 
🍞Food: 9/10 the food was delicious for the price, definitely felt like a great meal. agreed with dan that the fries needed a little salt LOL but overall it was so good. there are also so many options and they even offer all day breakfast, create your own salads, smoothies, and milkshakes!

overall, we’d definitely come back here again. this is a great, wallet-friendly option for a delicious and well rounded meal! definitely want to check out their location on spruce street and maybe even eat outdoors when it gets warmer again!
